driver: Six regional import corridors compete for a fixed annual capital remediation budget ranked by projected avoidable carrier-controllable cost per euro invested, where all three operational mechanisms are disclosed openly in the governance charter without specifying functional forms: an asymmetric convex upstream pull-back response where filling segregated cold-storage chambers throttles port yards far more steeply than draining chambers at the same occupancy while opposing produce seasons hold aggregate warehouse occupancy flat; a joint multivariate block-train model separating terminal-varying regulatory inspection booking lock cutoffs with stochastic pass-through from overlapping peak-day traction and consist cuts; and a conserved shipping-line empty-return queue stock that builds during episodic portal closures and persists across multi-day open drain tails scaled by inland haul distance.
driver_concrete: Weserfrucht Import GmbH allocates a fixed EUR 1,750,000 2027 carrier-remediation capital budget across six North Sea port-to-DC refrigerated import corridors (BHV-HAN, BHV-KAS, BHV-OSN, HAM-HAN, HAM-MAG, WHV-OSN) by Benefit-Cost Ratio (avoidable 2027 carrier-controllable EUR per EUR capex): reconstructing sealed +2C/+7C/+13C DC chamber stocks and estimating asymmetric convex filling-vs-draining hysteresis removes 7,436.9 c-days of DC pull-back (dropping BHV-KAS from naive #1 at 2.176 to #6 at 0.901); jointly modeling terminal-varying BIP lock cutoffs (BHV ~16h, HAM ~28h, WHV ~12h) alongside Nordbahn short-consist and loco-derate cuts removes 4,304.1 c-days of BIP rail bump (dropping HAM-MAG from naive #2 at 2.136 to #4 at 0.988); and conserving (port, shipping_line) empty-depot queue stock across open drain days removes 7,171.5 c-days of depot backlog (dropping BHV-HAN from naive #3 at 2.012 to #5 at 0.949), funding WHV-OSN (1.139), BHV-OSN (1.100), and HAM-HAN (1.086).
